waivers.justification: User decision 2026-10-25 (PR #328). Clock net u_cpu_pll_sub.u_ref_cm.mux_clk: a hard-instantiated clock mux (u_mux, mux2_4 from sky130_clkcells_stub) driving the hard-instantiated buf_16 root buffer u_root_buf, in the CTS clock-net set, plus 7 antenna diodes that OpenROAD.RepairAntennas inserted AFTER the cap repair stage (0 diodes on this net in RUN_2026-10-17_23-06-56; the diode attribution is inferred from the netlist and the log, not isolated by an experiment). Neither the pre-route nor the post-GRT cap-repair margin can reach it: raising GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_CAP_PCT 30 -> 40 (RUN_2026-10-25_15-59-23) left it at 0.379-0.418 pF against the 0.3397 pF limit. Measured in the shipped run RUN_2026-10-25_08-28-45: min_ss 0.3985, nom_ss 0.4210, max_ss 0.4356 pF (+17 to +28 percent over the limit); the other six corners do not violate. The driver is a stable hand-instantiated name, but the schema only accepts a driver waiver pinned to a run_id (no glob, no load pin: the net has no macro load), so this waiver goes STALE on any other run and must be re-issued or the schema extended.

User decision 2026-10-25 (PR #328). Write-data net u_sram.mb_din0_m[22] from the MBIST collar mux into the SRAM macro pin din0[22]. Measured in the shipped run RUN_2026-10-25_08-28-45: max_ss 0.3460 pF against the 0.3388 pF limit (+2.1 percent); no other corner violates. Ceiling = the next round 0.01 pF above the measurement (+1.2 percent), so a regression fails. Keyed on the load macro pin, not on the synthesis-generated driver. An over-repair run (GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_CAP_PCT 40, RUN_2026-10-25_15-59-23) cleared this net but raised unwaived max-cap from 8 to 23 (SRAM macro dout0 nets at all corners) and added a max_ss setup violator, so the shipped run keeps the margin at 30 and waives instead.
